SEASON

When this trip makes sense.

The December–January lake reference belongs to this operator’s northern Patagonia description. Do not apply it to every river, altitude or Chilean destination. Use Southern Hemisphere dates explicitly and obtain the intended water-by-water itinerary before specifying tackle.

JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec

Specific lake dragonfly reference, not entire trout season.

SET — Fly fishing Patagonia ↗

Design the week as distinct fishing days

Ask how many days are spent floating, wading spring creeks or fishing lakes and whether the plan changes with conditions. Choose variety deliberately rather than adding transfers for their own sake. A customer prioritizing sight-fishing should not discover that most days are long floats; one wanting less walking should state that before the itinerary is assembled.

Use line and fly systems by job

Ask whether the primary plan is dry-fly presentation, nymphing or streamer work. Match the outfit to that task and define the fallback explicitly. A spare spool or second supplied outfit may be more useful than a new rod for every destination name. Let the guide recommend fly sizes and line choices for the actual waters rather than shopping from a generic Patagonia assortment.

Plan the lodge-to-water logistics

Separate overnight luggage from the boat or walk-day bag. Confirm drying space, vehicle transfers and the equipment provided on each type of day. Camp-based floats add a different baggage and comfort decision from returning to a lodge. The same personal rain and insulation system can support several days, while technical tackle changes with the fishing.

LICENCE & PERMITS

Fishing licence for Argentina

Fishing permits depend on the province and water. Castward trips include Tierra del Fuego, Santa Cruz and Corrientes; do not treat one provincial permit as nationwide permission.

  • 1 dayARS 78000
  • 3 daysARS 117000
  • 7 daysARS 195000
  • 2026/27 seasonARS 260000
Official rules ↗

Rules for this water

  • The default 2026–27 season runs from 1 November to 1 May; the named-water annex can change these dates.
  • Release all fish in rivers and streams, including the regulated 200 m areas around their mouths and outlets.
  • Use a single barbless hook in mandatory catch-and-release waters.
  • Check the annex for the exact river or lake before fishing.
